periods.analysis: Summer Literacy Program Enrollment closed at 537 students, comfortably above the target of >=400 and a strong signal that families are using libraries and recreation sites as learning anchors, not just summer drop-off points. This quarter’s result gives us a healthy baseline for the arc ahead, especially with the Main Library, Harborview East Branch, and the Bayside Rec Center all filling morning literacy blocks by the second week of registration. Staff did good, resident-centered work by pairing reading circles with lunch service and airport-area shuttle Route L-3, which helped working families keep attendance practical.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the branch-and-rec-center model and reserve the first 60 seats next cycle for students referred by school attendance teams, so learning support reaches families before chronic absenteeism hardens. Extend the successful lunch-and-literacy pairing to one additional southside site and keep Route L-3 coordination in the registration packet.

periods.analysis: Enrollment moved down by 82 students quarter over quarter, from 537 to 455 students, but remained green and above the >=400 target. The decline is expected after the peak summer push, and it tells us families still stayed connected through fall intersession reading cohorts at North Pier Library and the Westhaven Community Room. I am encouraged that the number did not fall below target, because it means the summer relationships converted into a smaller but reliable learning pipeline for residents.
periods.recommendations: Keep the fall cohort structure, but tighten outreach to families who attended fewer than four summer sessions by assigning each branch a callback list from the CivicRec registration file. Sustain the North Pier and Westhaven cohorts, and add one Saturday family literacy lab in November to protect participation during school-year schedule pressure.

periods.analysis: Enrollment rose by 16 students quarter over quarter, from 455 to 471 students, again holding green against the >=400 target. That modest increase matters because Q1 is when transportation, school fatigue, and caregiver work schedules can quietly push children away from enrichment. The Library Learning Team’s Read Harborview winter challenge and the Parks teen aides at Maple Street and Seaport branches helped turn a maintenance quarter into forward movement for families.
periods.recommendations: Continue the Read Harborview challenge and give branch managers a shared weekly dashboard showing registrations, waitlists, and no-shows by site. Extend teen-aide coverage at Maple Street and Seaport through spring break, with a specific goal of converting waitlisted families into confirmed summer slots.

periods.analysis: Enrollment increased sharply by 91 students quarter over quarter, from 471 to 562 students, the strongest result in this sequence and well above the >=400 target. This is what good public operations look like when they become visible to residents: early school referrals, bilingual registration nights, and pop-up signups at the Ferry Market and Terminal 4 family resource fair all worked together. The lift also shows that our learning opportunity network is reaching beyond families who already know how to navigate city programs.
periods.recommendations: Sustain early registration nights and lock in bilingual staffing at the five highest-volume sites before the next enrollment window opens. Extend pop-up registration to the airport employee family day and the South Harbor housing resource clinic, and hold 25 contingency seats for late referrals from school chronic-absenteeism teams.

periods.analysis: Enrollment eased by 27 students quarter over quarter, from 562 to 535 students, while remaining green and solidly above the >=400 target. After the very strong Q2 surge, this is a healthy settling rather than a loss of momentum, particularly because the summer schedule still served full cohorts at Bayside Rec Center, Main Library, and the new Canal Point mobile library stop. Families benefited from the operational discipline behind the scenes: consistent rosters, text reminders, and shared reading kits made participation easier in a busy coastal city summer.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the text-reminder protocol and standardize reading-kit inventory so every site starts with the same materials by week one. Extend the Canal Point mobile stop for the full next cycle, and review the 27-student dip by site to see whether capacity, transportation, or family scheduling caused the softening.

periods.analysis: Enrollment declined by 85 students quarter over quarter, from 535 to 450 students, but stayed green and above the >=400 target. I read this as a watchful seasonal dip, not a program weakness, because fall participation always competes with school-year demands and caregiver shift changes tied to the port and airport economy. Still, the smaller cushion above target reminds us that access has to be actively maintained, especially for students who need steady literacy support outside the classroom.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the fall cohorts but add a retention protocol: two missed sessions should trigger a friendly call, not a quiet withdrawal. Extend evening pickup windows at Harborview East and South Harbor for six weeks, and ask school partners to refresh referrals for students with chronic-absenteeism flags before winter break.

periods.analysis: Enrollment rebounded by 21 students quarter over quarter, from 450 to 471 students, keeping the program green against the >=400 target. That recovery is important because it shows the fall retention work is beginning to stabilize the pipeline into the next summer season. Branch staff reported stronger re-enrollment from families reached through the missed-session calls, and the South Harbor evening window appears to have made the program more workable for caregivers on nontraditional shifts.
periods.recommendations: Keep the missed-session call protocol and make it part of the standard operating checklist for every literacy site. Extend the South Harbor evening window through spring registration, and create a small re-enrollment cohort for the 2025 participants who attended inconsistently but remained reachable.

periods.analysis: Enrollment climbed by 87 students quarter over quarter, from 471 to 558 students, once again well above the >=400 target and nearly matching the prior year’s Q2 high of 562 students. The two-year pattern is now clear: when we start early, meet families where they already are, and remove small barriers, participation follows. This quarter’s gains came from practical resident-facing work, including school backpack flyers, library-card signups at the Seaport Family Expo, and coordinated rosters between Parks instructors and library youth services staff.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the early, multi-site registration strategy and protect staffing for the high-demand Main, Bayside, Harborview East, and South Harbor locations. Extend the Seaport Family Expo signup model to the airport community fair, and set a stretch planning assumption of at least 560 seats next Q2 while preserving the >=400 performance floor.

periods.analysis: Summer literacy enrollment is above target at 570 against 400, and enrollment has opened. The summer-session launch is still 70% complete, so the briefing should distinguish access to sign-up from delivery of the full program.
periods.recommendations: Verify staffing and site readiness before reporting the launch as complete, then review attendance alongside enrollment.
